spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

## ¶2

All these affections that are perceived in the mind, and also the remaining living states [GAP-1] of the external natural mind — these are established according to three modes of spiritual formation [GAP-2]: some arise from [GAP-3] abortive and incomplete spiritual births. Others, however, take on their own form according to their inherent spiritual quality [GAP-4].

## ¶3

Also, their spiritual sustenance is thre[GAP-5: efold — the] wisdom dwelling within them, if they shall desire to receive it [GAP-6]. [GAP-7] They take in interior truths and the good works produced from them [GAP-8]; they receive interior truths and goods of use. The [GAP-9] it entirely, and they [GAP-10] the three fundamental spiritual patterns inherent in their nature and the [GAP-11] the period during which they dwell in the external natural mind [GAP-12]; they are held captive [GAP-13] in their [GAP-14]. The Divine Emissary [GAP-15] all governing loves [GAP-16].

## ¶4

[GAP-17: REVIEW N] it [GAP-18], first [GAP-19]. Establish them generally under this designation: nascent perceptions and elementary natural knowledges. It formed the evil, falsified perceptions — the hollow semblances of truth, the falsities that wound and pierce — and the [GAP-20] and all others that resemble them.

## ¶5

For that intention belongs to the ruling loves of self that devour living affections. Still, these [GAP-21: REVIEW that were] established pertain to elementary natural knowledges and simple natural goods, since they exist within their own essential nature. Nevertheless, that intention which descended from the ruling loves — insofar as it manifests first in works of use and natural knowledges and has not yet been implanted into what is corporeal and of the proprium — it formed the perceptions that yield nourishing goods of use, just as their natural goods are genuinely sweet and life-giving.

## ¶6

Again, that intention which descended from the governing loves that devour living affections and also consume natural knowledges and simple natural goods — it has formed the perceptions that yield no spiritual nourishment whatsoever. Their works belong neither to genuine good nor to manifest evil.

---

**Translator's note:** The threefold structure throughout concerns three degrees of spiritual formation determined by the quality of the ruling love from which they descend: (1) loves oriented toward devouring affections (pure self-love) produce perceptions bearing only falsity and harm; (2) loves that also feed on natural knowledges and simple goods produce perceptions bearing neither good nor evil — spiritually barren states; (3) loves that operate within natural knowledges *before* descending into the corporeal proprium produce perceptions that yield genuinely nourishing goods. The "abortions" of ¶2 are spiritual states that never reach full formation because the ruling love is too disordered to carry them to completion.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: All these animals that you see, and also the rest of the [crea]tures [upon the face] of the earth, confirm them in three likeness[es of birth]: some from [the] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [and nature].

Also, their nourishment is thre[efold: the] light in them, if they shall wish [to eat it]. [Some of them] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit and grass]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [nourishment fills] it entirely, and they [bear within them] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [whole of] the time when they are on the ea[rth in this world]; they are seized [and bound] in their [bodies]. The Ambassador [purifies] all powers [of the darkness].

[Now] it [formed them], first [of all]. Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [thistles] and these others that are like them.

For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.

Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.

fills.explanation: The phrase "creatures upon the face of the earth" is a standard Manichaean/biblical formula for terrestrial beings dwelling in the external natural plane.
The spiritual reading indicates "modes of spiritual formation," and "likenesses of birth" directly frames the subsequent enumeration of abortive births versus self-formed creatures.
"Some from the abortions" uses the standard definite article referencing the well-known Manichaean cosmological category of the rulers' abortive offspring.

The spiritual reading specifies "inherent spiritual quality," which in the Kephalaia's natural register corresponds to "nature" — the inherent quality that determines the creature's self-formed shape.
The spiritual reading confirms "threefold — the wisdom" and in the Kephalaia's register "the light" is the natural-plane equivalent of wisdom, yielding "threefold: the light in them."
The spiritual reading says "desire to receive it"; in the nourishment context of the Kephalaia, "eating" is the natural-plane action of receiving spiritual sustenance (light).
The threefold nourishment structure requires categorical introductions; "Some of them" initiates the first dietary type, paralleling "some from" in ¶2's threefold classification.

The threefold dietary distinction requires differentiating this first group (seeds, fruit, AND grass) from the second (seeds and fruit only), paralleling the ¶5–6 distinction between grass-eating and flesh-eating rulers.

Echoing "their nourishment is threefold" from the paragraph's opening, "The nourishment fills it entirely" states that the light-sustenance pervades each creature completely before they manifest the three archetypes.

The spiritual reading indicates creatures carry "three fundamental spiritual patterns inherent in their nature"; "bear within them" is the natural-plane expression for carrying interior archetypal forms.
The spiritual reading says "the period during which they dwell"; "the whole of the time" indicates the entire duration of their earthly existence during which the archetypes and captivity persist.
The Kephalaia commonly specifies "on the earth in this world" as the locative for the mixed realm of light and darkness — the external natural plane of incarnate existence.
The spiritual reading says "held captive"; in Manichaean cosmology, light-elements are "seized and bound" in matter — a standard doublet expressing the captivity of the divine within corporeal forms.
In Manichaean cosmology, the light-particles are trapped "in their bodies" — the material forms of creatures constitute the prison in which the divine elements are bound.
The Ambassador (Third Messenger) acts to extract and purify the trapped light from the archonic powers; "purifies" captures his cosmological role of separating light from the mixture of darkness.
"All powers of the darkness" is a standard Kephalaia designation for the archonic forces; the Ambassador's purifying action targets the powers that belong to the realm of darkness.
The editor's "N" is the beginning of "Now," a standard paragraph-transitional conjunction in Kephalaia translations corresponding to a Coptic discourse particle.
The paragraph repeatedly uses "it formed" (the ruling intention formed various plants); "Now it formed them" introduces the general act of plant-formation that the paragraph then specifies.
"First of all" is a standard introductory formula in the Kephalaia, establishing the general category (shoots and grass) before the specific enumeration of plant types that follows.
In the catalogue of harmful plants (reeds, thorns, and...), "thistles" completes the standard triad of wounding/piercing vegetation corresponding to falsities that injure in the spiritual sense.

Confirming the editor's choice: "these that were planted" is grammatically correct and corresponds to the spiritual reading's "these that were established," maintaining the passive construction linking planted things to their ruling origin.
